# eci_load_balancer (Resource)

Load Balancer

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "eci_pricing" "lb_pricing" {
  name         = "Load Balancer"
  pricing_type = "ondemand"
}

data "eci_pricing" "ip_pricing" {
  name         = "Public IP"
  pricing_type = "ondemand"
}

# A load balancer needs a public ip that is not attached to a network interface.
resource "eci_public_ip" "lb_ip" {
  dr         = false
  pricing_id = data.eci_pricing.ip_pricing.id
  tags       = {}
}

resource "eci_load_balancer" "my_load_balancer" {
  name                = "web"
  attached_network_id = "0f4c2a3e-2a31-4b8e-9a51-8d1f8c0c6b10"
  public_ip_id        = eci_public_ip.lb_ip.id
  pricing_id          = data.eci_pricing.lb_pricing.id

  rules = [
    {
      proto     = "TCP"
      port      = 80
      algorithm = "roundrobin"
      servers = [
        {
          ip                   = "10.0.0.11"
          network_interface_id = "4adf2682-d8f3-451c-8bfc-3383deb424a5"
          port                 = 8080
        },
      ]
      healthcheck = {
        proto               = "HTTP"
        port                = 8080
        path                = "/healthz"
        interval            = 5
        timeout             = 3
        healthy_threshold   = 2
        unhealthy_threshold = 3
      }
    },
  ]

  tags = {
    "created-by" : "terraform"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `attached_network_id` (String) id of virtual network that the load balancer attaches to
- `name` (String) name of the load balancer
- `pricing_id` (String) id of pricing plan for the load balancer
- `public_ip_id` (String) id of public ip assigned to the load balancer
- `rules` (Attributes List) forwarding rules of the load balancer (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules))
- `tags` (Map of String) User-defined metadata of key-value pairs

### Read-Only

- `activated` (String) the time when the load balancer is activated
- `created` (String) the time when the load balancer is created
- `deleted` (String) the time when the load balancer is deleted
- `id` (String) unique identifier of the load balancer
- `kubernetes_cluster_id` (String) id of kubernetes cluster that owns the load balancer, if any
- `modified` (String) the last time when the load balancer is modified
- `organization_id` (String) id of organization that the load balancer belongs to
- `pricing_type` (String) type of pricing plan (computed)
- `short_id` (String) short identifier of the load balancer
- `status` (String) status of the load balancer
- `zone_id` (String) id of zone that the load balancer belongs to

<a id="nestedatt--rules"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules`

Required:

- `algorithm` (String) balancing algorithm (roundrobin, random or leastconn)
- `healthcheck` (Attributes) health check of the servers in the rule (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--healthcheck))
- `port` (Number) port that the load balancer listens on
- `proto` (String) protocol of the rule (TCP or UDP)
- `servers` (Attributes List) backend servers of the rule (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--rules--servers))

<a id="nestedatt--rules--healthcheck"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.healthcheck`

Required:

- `healthy_threshold` (Number) consecutive successes to mark a server healthy
- `interval` (Number) seconds between health checks
- `port` (Number) health check port
- `proto` (String) health check protocol (TCP or HTTP)
- `timeout` (Number) seconds before a health check times out
- `unhealthy_threshold` (Number) consecutive failures to mark a server unhealthy

Optional:

- `path` (String) HTTP health check path, starting with /


<a id="nestedatt--rules--servers"></a>
### Nested Schema for `rules.servers`

Required:

- `ip` (String) private ip of the backend server
- `network_interface_id` (String) id of network interface of the backend server
- `port` (Number) port of the backend server
